question: Schedule VII of the Indian Constitution contains —
solution:
The correct answer is __**Three legislative lists**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Schedule VII** of the **Indian Constitution** categorically deals with the division of powers between the **Union and the State Governments**.
 
• It contains the **Three legislative lists**, namely the **Union List**, the **State List**, and the **Concurrent List**. These lists specify the subjects on which respective governments can legislate.
 
• **Union List:** This list includes subjects on which only the **Parliament** can make laws. Examples include defense, foreign affairs, atomic energy, and banking.
 
• **State List:** This list includes subjects on which only the **State Legislatures** can make laws. Examples include police, public health, agriculture, and local government.
 
• **Concurrent List:** This list includes subjects on which both the **Parliament** and the **State Legislatures** can legislate. Examples include education, marriage, bankruptcy, and trade unions.
 
• The division of legislative powers ensures a federal structure by defining the areas of governance for both levels of government.
 
• *Hence, Schedule VII of the Indian Constitution contains the Three legislative lists.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Union List:**

 
 
• The **Union List** currently has **97 subjects**. The Union Government has exclusive power to legislate on these subjects.
 
• Some important subjects in the Union List include **defense**, **foreign affairs**, **currency**, **railways**, and **citizenship**.
 
 
 
• **State List:**
 
 
• The **State List** includes **61 subjects**. The State Legislatures have exclusive power to legislate on these subjects unless the Constitution provides otherwise.
 
• Subjects like **land**, **agriculture**, **police**, and **local government** are included in the State List.
 
 
 
• **Concurrent List:**
 
 
• The **Concurrent List** consists of **52 subjects**. Both the Union and State Governments can legislate on these subjects.
 
• In case of conflict, the law enacted by the **Union Government** prevails over the State law.
 
• Subjects like **education**, **trade unions**, and **criminal law** fall under the Concurrent List.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Schedule VII:**
 
 
• Schedule VII is crucial for maintaining the **federal structure** of India by clearly defining the legislative areas of the Union and State Governments.
 
• It reduces the chances of overlapping legislation and ensures administrative efficiency.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Background:**

 
 
• The **Government of India Act, 1935** served as the foundation for the legislative division in Schedule VII.
 
• The act introduced the concept of federalism by categorizing subjects into lists, which was later adopted in the Constitution of India.
 
 
 
• **Amendments:**
 
 
• The **42nd Amendment Act, 1976** added subjects like education and forests to the Concurrent List.
 
• Certain subjects have been moved between lists based on socio-economic and political requirements.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Interpretation:**
 
 
• The judiciary has played a crucial role in resolving conflicts arising due to overlapping subjects between the Union and State Lists.
 
• The principle of federal supremacy ensures that Union laws prevail in case of conflict.
